Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

by preposition

a time: not later than

also by January, by tomorrow, by then, by now, by what date?, by nightfall, around the time of, at about the same time

classical

Cic. Fam. 16.10.4: nostra ad diem dictam fient (Lewis & Short s.v. ad)
Caes. BG 2.5: omnia ad diem facta sunt (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 86: by January, ad mēnsem Jānuārium; by the sixth hour, ad sextam hōram
Traupman 285

ad + acc.

by, on (a set time)

What is due or done by a set day: ad diem, on the day, punctually. “By now” is jam (see already).

Other words

  • sub + acc. — towards, around (a time), just before

    also used · classical · Liv. 42.45.1: lēgātiō sub idem tempus in Asiam et circum īnsulās missa (Lewis & Short s.v. sub); Traupman 88: around the time of, sub tempus (+ gen.); at about the same time, sub idem tempus; Traupman 394

    Close to a time, on either side of it: sub noctem, towards nightfall (see just before nightfall).

Examples

  • quam ad diem legiōnī frūmentum dēbērī sciēbat

    the day on which, as he knew, corn was due to the legionCaes. BG 6.33 (Lewis & Short s.v. dēbeō)

  • ad mēnsem Jānuārium

    by JanuaryTraupman 86

  • Quam ad diem?

    By what date?Traupman 86

  • ad proximam noctem

    by the following nightTraupman 85

  • sub idem tempus

    at about the same timeTraupman 88

See also until, before, just before nightfall, already, due.
